title: AI Glossary: 60 Generative AI Terms Explained Simply — cv.cm
description: An AI glossary of 60 essential terms, from tokens, LoRA and RAG to diffusion, CFG, voice cloning, C2PA and deepfakes, each with a plain meaning and an example.
h1: AI glossary: generative AI terms explained
answer: This glossary explains about 60 terms you meet when using generative AI, grouped by topic: models and training, text and LLMs, image and video generation, audio, and safety and law. Each entry gives a plain meaning and a short example, so you can decode a model card, a settings panel or a news story without a technical background.

body: These terms describe what a model is and how it gets built. They apply to text, image, video and audio models alike.

head: Term
Meaning
Example
rows: Artificial intelligence (AI)
Software that performs tasks that normally need human intelligence
Translation, face unlock, a chat assistant
Machine learning
AI that learns patterns from examples instead of following hand-written rules
A spam filter trained on labeled emails
Neural network
A model made of many layers of simple connected units whose strengths are learned
The core of every modern image or language model
Model
The trained network itself, a file of learned numbers plus the code to run it
An app such as a chatbot runs one or more models
Parameters (weights)
The numbers inside a model that training adjusts
A 7B model has about 7 billion parameters
Training data
The examples a model learns from
Web text, licensed books, image and caption pairs
Pretraining
The first, largest training stage on broad data
Learning to predict the next token on web-scale text
Fine-tuning
Further training of an existing model on a smaller, focused dataset
Training a base model on customer-support answers
LoRA
Low-rank adaptation: a small add-on file that fine-tunes a model cheaply without changing the original weights
A style or character LoRA for an image model
Foundation model
A large general model that many products and fine-tunes are built on
One LLM powering chat, search and coding tools
Open-weight model
A model whose weights can be downloaded and run yourself; the license may still limit use
Running an open model on your own computer
Inference
Running a trained model to get an output
Each time you press Generate
Quantization
Storing weights with fewer bits to make a model smaller and faster, with a small quality loss
A 4-bit version of a model that fits on a laptop
Multimodal model
A model that handles more than one type of data, such as text and images
Asking a question about a photo

body: Terms you see in chat apps, API settings and articles about LLMs.

head: Term
Meaning
Example
rows: Large language model (LLM)
A large neural network trained to predict the next token of text
The model behind ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, DeepSeek, Qwen
Token
The unit of text a model reads and writes: a word, part of a word or a symbol
unbelievable can be 3 tokens: un, bel, ievable
Context window
The maximum number of tokens a model can consider at once, input plus output
A long chat that starts forgetting its beginning
Transformer
The neural network design, based on attention, used by almost all LLMs
GPT means Generative Pre-trained Transformer
Attention
The step that lets each token weigh which earlier tokens matter to it
Linking it to trophy in a sentence about a suitcase
Embedding
A list of numbers that represents meaning, so similar texts get similar numbers
Finding documents similar to a question
Prompt
The input you give a model
Summarize this email in two sentences
System prompt
Hidden instructions set by the app or developer before the conversation
You are a polite support agent for a bike shop
Temperature
A setting that controls randomness in the output
Low for data extraction, higher for brainstorming
Hallucination
A confident but false or invented statement from a model
A citation to a paper that does not exist
RAG (retrieval-augmented generation)
Searching documents first and putting the best passages in the prompt
A help bot that answers from your manuals
Knowledge cutoff
The date after which the model has no training data
It does not know about last month's events
Reasoning mode
A mode where the model writes intermediate steps before the final answer
Shown as thinking in some chat apps
Tool use (function calling)
The model asks the app to run a tool and reads the result
Calling a calculator or web search
AI agent
A system where a model plans and takes several tool actions toward a goal
Researching and booking options across websites

body: Settings and techniques that appear in image and video tools such as Midjourney, Stable Diffusion, FLUX, Veo, Kling, Runway and Seedance. Names differ slightly between tools.

head: Term
Meaning
Example
rows: Diffusion model
A model that creates an image by removing noise step by step from random noise
Most text-to-image tools
Latent space
A compressed internal representation where the model works instead of on raw pixels
Latent diffusion generates a small latent, then decodes it to an image
Text-to-image
Generating an image from a text prompt
A red bicycle against a blue wall at sunset
Image-to-image
Generating a new image guided by an input image
Turning a sketch into a finished illustration
Inpainting
Regenerating only a masked area of an image
Replacing a coffee cup on a table with a plant
Negative prompt
Text describing what to avoid
blurry, extra fingers, watermark
Seed
The starting random number; the same seed and settings give a similar result
Reusing a seed to make small prompt changes
Guidance scale (CFG)
How strongly the output follows the prompt versus looking natural
Too high gives harsh colors and artifacts
ControlNet
An add-on that guides a diffusion model with a pose, edge or depth image
Keeping a character's exact pose
Depth map
A grayscale image where brightness shows distance from the camera
Used for parallax video and ControlNet
Upscaling
Enlarging an image with a model that adds plausible detail
A 512-pixel image enlarged 4 times
Text-to-video
Generating a video clip from a text prompt
A paper boat drifting down a rainy street
Image-to-video
Animating a still image into a clip
Making a product photo slowly rotate
First and last frame
Giving a start image and an end image and letting the model fill the motion between
A door closed in the first frame and open in the last

head: Term
Meaning
Example
rows: Speech-to-text (ASR)
Automatic speech recognition: turning spoken audio into text
Transcribing a meeting or a video
Whisper
A widely used open speech recognition model family from OpenAI
Making subtitles in many languages
Text-to-speech (TTS)
Turning text into spoken audio
Reading an article aloud
Voice cloning
A TTS model that imitates a specific person's voice from a sample
A voiceover in the creator's own voice, with consent
Speaker diarization
Labeling who spoke when in a recording
Speaker 1 and Speaker 2 in an interview transcript
Word error rate (WER)
The share of words a transcript gets wrong, used to measure ASR quality
A WER of 5 percent means about 1 wrong word in 20
SRT and VTT
Plain-text subtitle formats with timestamps for each line
Uploading captions to a video platform

body: Rules differ by country and change often. This section is general information, not legal advice.

head: Term
Meaning
Example
rows: Deepfake
Realistic AI-generated or AI-altered media that shows people or events that are not real
A video of a politician saying words they never said
Content credentials (C2PA)
An open standard that attaches signed information about how a file was made and edited
A photo showing it was edited with an AI tool
Invisible watermark
A hidden signal embedded in pixels or audio that software can detect later
A generator marking every image it makes
Explicit and implicit labels
In China's labeling rules: a visible label people can see, and a hidden label in metadata or a watermark
An AI-generated tag on a video plus a metadata field
EU AI Act transparency duties
EU rules that people must be told when they talk to an AI, and that AI content and deepfakes must be identifiable
A chatbot disclosing it is a bot
Training data copyright
The legal question of whether training on copyrighted works is allowed, which differs by country
Lawsuits and policy reports in several countries
Guardrails
Rules and filters that block harmful requests or outputs
Refusing to give instructions for weapons
Jailbreak
A prompt crafted to make a model ignore its safety rules
A role-play trick to bypass refusals
Prompt injection
Hidden instructions in a web page or file that hijack an AI that reads it
A page that tells an AI agent to send your data elsewhere
Bias
Systematic unfairness in outputs, often learned from skewed training data
Images of a profession that show only one gender

body: Several pairs of terms are confused in news stories and product pages. The difference usually changes what you should do.

head: Pair
Difference
Why it matters
rows: Model vs app
The model generates; the app adds the interface, system prompt, tools and storage
Two apps on the same model can behave differently
Token vs word
A word can be one token or several; counts differ by language
Prices and limits are counted in tokens
Parameters vs context window
Parameters are what the model learned; the context window is what it can see right now
A huge model can still forget the start of a long chat
Fine-tuning vs RAG
Fine-tuning changes the model; RAG gives it documents at question time
For facts that change often, RAG is usually easier
Open-weight vs open-source
Open weights can be downloaded; open source also means the training code and data are open under an open license
Read the license before commercial use
Watermark vs label
A watermark is a technical signal; a label is a disclosure people can read
Some laws require both

body: For a deeper explanation of any term, see the related articles in this section, such as how LLMs work, tokens and the context window, and how diffusion models work.

faq.q: What is the difference between AI, machine learning and deep learning?
faq.a: AI is the whole field. Machine learning is the part of AI that learns from examples. Deep learning is the part of machine learning that uses many-layered neural networks, which is what modern generative models are.

faq.q: What is the difference between an LLM and a chatbot?
faq.a: An LLM is the model that generates text. A chatbot is an app built around one or more models, adding a chat interface, instructions, memory features and tools such as web search.

faq.q: What does open source mean for AI models?
faq.a: It is used loosely. Often it means only that the weights can be downloaded. A fully open model also shares training code and data details under an open license. Check the license for commercial use and attribution rules.

faq.q: What does 7B or 70B mean in a model name?
faq.a: It is the approximate number of parameters, in billions. A larger number usually means more capability but also more memory and computing power to run it.

faq.q: Is prompt engineering a real skill?
faq.a: Yes, in the practical sense of writing clear, specific instructions, giving examples and supplying the right context. Models keep improving at understanding plain requests, but clear input still gives more reliable output.
